newsitem.title: FRANCE: Suspected Corsican separatist chief sent to Paris.
newsitem.headline: Suspected Corsican separatist chief sent to Paris.

text.p: Police flew a suspected leader of the outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC) to Paris on Wednesday as a crackdown continued against separatist guerrillas on the troubled Mediterranean island.

Officials said Jean-Michel Rossi, a leading member of A Cuncolta Naziunalista, the legal facade of the FLNC, was to be questioned by magistrates investigating some of the hundreds of bomb attacks on the island in the past two years.
Rossi is editor of the stridently nationalist newspaper U Ribombu (The Thunderclap) which has itself been investigated for possible legal action over alleged threats contained in its columns.

He is the third leading member of A Cuncolta to be detained in the past few weeks in a crackdown which was stepped up after FLNC guerrillas bombed the mayoral office of Prime Minister Alain Juppe in Bordeaux last month.
The head of A Cuncolta, Francois Santoni, and his lawyer girlfriend, Marie-Helene Mattei, have been held since last month.
Rossi, who had been in hiding for weeks, gave himself up on Tuesday after police arrested some 15 members or sympathisers of Conculta in raids in Corsica and southern France on Monday.
Police said they seized sawn-off shotguns, pistols, revolvers, a grenade and ammunition in the raids, spurred by an inquiry into the bombing of a hotel complex in northern Corsica in October
